meta.title: Operation of HPLC System in Pharmaceutics Laboratory

sections.purpose: To perform High Performance Liquid Chromatography for quantitative assay, purity determination, and content uniformity testing of pharmaceutical formulations as per validated pharmacopeial and in-house analytical methods.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmaceutics laboratory for drug content assay in tablets, capsules, and liquid formulations, and for related substance determination as part of product quality control.
procedure: Switch on the HPLC pump, detector (UV/PDA), column oven, and autosampler; open the workstation software.
Allow the system to warm up for 20–30 minutes before analysis.
Prepare mobile phase as per the validated method: filter through 0.45 µm membrane filter and degas by sonication for 15 minutes.
Prime all mobile phase lines: purge each pump head for 5 minutes to remove air bubbles.
Flush the column with the starting mobile phase composition at 1 mL/min for at least 15–20 column volumes.
Set the column oven temperature as per the method (typically 25–40°C).
Set detector wavelength as per the validated method.
Establish a stable baseline — wait until drift is < 0.001 AU/min for UV detection.
Prepare sample and standard solutions as per the method: dissolve in the specified diluent; filter through 0.45 µm PTFE filter before injection.
Inject the system suitability solution: verify theoretical plates (N ≥ 2000), tailing factor (≤ 2.0), and resolution (≥ 2.0 for adjacent peaks).
Inject blank, standard, and then sample solutions in sequence.
Calculate drug content: % assay = (Area of sample / Area of standard) × (Standard concentration / Sample concentration) × Label claim × 100.
After analysis: flush column with mobile phase, then with 60–70% methanol/water, then store in methanol/acetonitrile.
Record all system suitability parameters, peak areas, retention times, and calculated results in the analytical register.
precautions: Filter all mobile phases and samples through 0.45 µm filters — particulates block the HPLC column and pump check valves irreversibly.
Degas mobile phases thoroughly — dissolved gases cause baseline noise and ghost peaks.
Never switch the pump off abruptly while at high pressure — always reduce flow gradually.
Use HPLC-grade solvents only — analytical grade solvents contain UV-absorbing impurities.
Flush the column with at least 10 column volumes after a high-salt buffer analysis before switching to organic mobile phase.
Never allow a reversed-phase column to run dry — introduces air and permanently damages the stationary phase.
Document all system suitability results — failing system suitability invalidates the entire run.
